info.title: pivotkit REST
info.summary: Describe data sources, validate and render pivot views, make links and draft schedules.
info.description: The operations of pivotkit's MCP server over HTTP for programs. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details. The routes are RPC-style (POST /views/validate); /api/v1 changes only with a breaking change. Docs: https://pivotkit.eize.dev/reference/rest/

tags.name: sources
tags.description: The data sources a caller may use.

tags.name: views
tags.description: Views: the guide, validation, description, rendering and links.

tags.name: schedules
tags.description: Drafts of scheduled reports for a person to approve.

get.description: The data sources this caller may use: id, title, whether a link or a schedule works for them.

post.description: A source's fields: name, type, level, counts, the aggregators and filter types each works with, and example views. Values (items, smallest and largest) only for fields the policy shows.

example.text: 2000 rows, 2 fields (1 more hidden by the operator)

post.description: A draft view made from a source's fields by fixed rules (rows a text field with few values, columns a date by its span, values the first number that is no identifier, summed), with what each part took and why (picks). A layout replaces the parts it gives. Check the draft before you render it.

view.name: Draft: Average of Sales by Region

example.name: Draft: Average of Sales by Region

picks.text: Region: the first text field with few values

get.description: The format of a view in short: its keys, the aggregators, filter types and date groupings, and example views.

example.text: A view is JSON: rows, cols, values, filters, ...

post.description: Checks a view against a source: errors and warnings with where they are and, for a misspelt name, the name meant (suggestion).
What a view shows and filters, in plain parts, with the same findings as validate.

post.summary: Render a view into the output directory
post.description: Runs a view (or a layout: a view by field names) over a source and saves the report (xlsx by default; html, csv, json, svg) in the server's output directory. A view with errors answers 200 with ok: false and its findings. csv and json come back inline only where the operator allows it (rest.inline).

example.message: The report is saved as Sum of Sales by Region.xlsx in the output directory.

post.summary: Create a link to a view
post.description: A link that opens the view in the source's report page, where a person sees the data with their own rights. Only for sources with link: true; a view with errors gets no link.

200.description: Create a link to a view

post.description: Writes a draft for a report that runs on a schedule. It runs nothing and sends nothing: a person approves the draft in the host. Recipients are names the host knows, never addresses.

example.message: The draft "Weekly sales" is ready for approval, saved as Weekly sales.report.json in the output directory. Nothing runs until a person approves it in the host.

get.summary: Describe a data source by its id
get.description: A source's fields: name, type, level, counts, the aggregators and filter types each works with, and example views. Values (items, smallest and largest) only for fields the policy shows. The same as POST /sources/describe.

example.text: 2000 rows, 2 fields (1 more hidden by the operator)

post.summary: Render a view and download the file
post.description: Runs a view over a source and answers with the file itself (Content-Disposition: attachment). Allowed only for callers whose policy profile has results: true; a view with errors answers 422 with its findings.

200.description: The file (json, csv, xlsx, svg, html), as an attachment.

type.description: The address that names the error's code.

code.description: A stable code; new ones may come. Today: INVALID_INPUT, FILES_NOT_ALLOWED, NOT_ALLOWED, SOURCE_NOT_FOUND, FILE_NOT_AVAILABLE, NO_OUTPUT, NO_LINK, NOT_SCHEDULABLE, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT, INVALID_FILE, NOT_REGULAR_FILE, HARD_LINK, INVALID_TEMPLATE, BUSY, NOT_READY, TIMEOUT, INTERNAL, INVALID_TOKEN, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, FORBIDDEN_HOST, FORBIDDEN_ORIGIN, NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, BODY_TOO_LARGE, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, VIEW_HAS_ERRORS, RATE_LIMITED, AUTH_NOT_READY.

detail.description: What went wrong and what to do; never file content.

findings.description: The view's findings (422 of the file route).

View.title: pivotkit view, version 2
View.description: A pivotkit view: the report's layout as JSON. Names are resolved against the data by pivotkit-core's normalize(), which also checks what a schema cannot (a field's name and type, an aggregator for a field). Built by scripts/schemas.js from pivotkit-core's tables. See https://pivotkit.eize.dev/concepts/views/

version.description: A view without a version is read as version 1.

items.description: The items, as the data has them; a blank is no item (see blanks).

not.description: Inverts which items with a value the filter keeps; blanks are decided by blanks alone.

blanks.description: What happens to blank items: exclude (the default) drops them, include keeps them too, only keeps them alone.

on.description: value: a text field's own value; label: the label the table shows (any field).

match.description: How text is folded before it is compared; default insensitive and collapse.

value.description: A number (also as text, "2022") or a date "2022-03-01".

precision.description: Dates only: both sides as the start of their unit; default day.

not.description: Inverts which items with a value the filter keeps; blanks are decided by blanks alone.

calendar.description: true (the default): whole units; false: rolling from now.

includeCurrent.description: With calendar: whether the current unit counts; default true.

anchor.description: What the range counts from: today (the default), latest, first, or a date.

Problem401.description: No token, or one the service does not accept (INVALID_TOKEN).

Problem403.description: Not allowed: a scope missing, files by path, a host or origin refused.

Problem409.description: The server cannot do this: no output directory, no link page, not schedulable.

Problem413.description: A limit: the body, the file or the result is too large.

Problem415.description: The body is not JSON, or the file's format is not read.

Problem422.description: The file cannot be read, or (file route) the view has errors.

Problem429.description: Too many requests: wait as Retry-After says.

Problem503.description: Busy or not ready: try again as Retry-After says.

Problem504.description: The report took longer than the server allows.

bearer.description: A static token the operator gives you: Authorization: Bearer <token>.
